_comment: Everything HELD CONSTANT across all twelve conditions of the grid lives
here, and only here. The twelve condition files extend this one and override
exactly three keys: chunk_size, retrieval_strategy and
indexing_representation. That is the vary-one-thing-at-a-time rule enforced
by the file layout rather than by discipline -- a value that ought to be
constant has literally one place to be written.
JSON, not YAML, so no dependency is added: every library is pinned in
requirements.txt and PyYAML is not among them.
_retrieval_scope_note: 'corpus' = every chunk of all 128 transcripts is a candidate. The alternative, scoping candidates to each question's own transcript_ids, would make retrieval trivially easy and would measure nothing about retrieval design. Recorded explicitly because it changes every number in the results.
query_prefix: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:
_indexing_representation_note: The THIRD independent variable is indexing_representation, set per condition file. Everything below is the FROZEN definition of what 'metadata_enriched' means -- format 'P2', signed off 2026-09-05 before any enriched run, per README.md invariant 2. Each value is cross-checked against its module constant in src/index.py by run_experiment.validate_config_matches_code, exactly the way query_prefix is: the config and the code that implements it cannot drift apart silently. Do not revise any of it after seeing results.
_max_content_tokens_note: bge-small-en-v1.5's max_seq_length is 512 (measured, and asserted against the loaded model in index.get_embedding_model), minus [CLS] and [SEP]. The enriched index_text is truncated to this budget at BUILD time, not left to the encoder: the encoder silently drops the overflow while BM25 has no length limit, so an untruncated enriched string would hand the two retrievers identical bytes but feed them different content -- confounding indexing representation with retrieval strategy in the 500-token enriched cell. Truncation reduces retrievability only: anchor matching runs against raw chunk['text'], which is never truncated.
_similarity_metric_note: The design leaves this as 'cosine over embeddings, or BERTScore'. Cosine over the retrieval embedding model is what evaluate.answer_similarity implements; see its docstring for why. Held constant across the grid either way.
